This is an initial reaction, as the item came today. My particular problem is that I have a hot tub that was allowed to cool off when a breaker tripped. It has been very cold here, and I was lucky to catch it in time. I thought it would be a good idea to get a device to monitor the temperature from inside, and I bought this and a Ambient Weather F007PF 8-Channel Wireless Pool and Spa Remote Sensor, and another regular sensor for a dome to cover the hot tub which will be arriving shortly.

These all run on AAA batteries, not included. The set up is easy, using DIP switches like the old garage door clickers. Everything lit up properly when the batteries were put in. There are LEDs on the remote sensors to confirm proper operation. The display on the remote sensors has a Channel indicator, so you can see that you have it right. My hot tub is on Channel 1, which works out well. The backlight can change colors based on the indoor temperature, or the temperature of the sensor on Channel 1. The default color for more than 100*F is red, and it changes to orange if the temperature of the hot tub drops below that. So with a casual glance across the room I can verify that the power is on, and the heater is functioning.

The display is big and bright, and the level of backlight can be easily adjusted. Like other LED displays, there are some angles from which the display cannot be read, mostly below straight on.

I purchased this to replace the WS11 model I had to return due to being defective. This one offers similar functions at a cheaper price. It can be customized to a limited degree and works with additional sensors (even ones from this company's other consoles). Accuracy can be calibrated with other more precise thermometers. It comes with both a battery-only function (but no batteries) and AC adapter. One complaint is that the power cord protrudes straight out from the bottom right side of the console and would be better served if it was angled at 90 degrees instead. The assorted color screens can always stay on when AC power is applied and only shows when prompted while on battery power alone to conserve the 4 AA batteries. I believe this function can be changed to be always on when on battery power but it will shorten their life. These screens can be programed to change with variations in temperature range both for Inside and Outside readings. My biggest complaint is the lack of hardware for wall-hanging this device and its sensors, especially the remote sensors which use a very small screw for hanging. I had a hard time finding these screws with accompanying wall anchors at the local hardware store. The lack of appropriate hardware, lack of power adapter cord angle along with what I found to be non-existent customer service for these devices caused it to lose that coveted 5th star.

Marvelous! We've tried/tested several different devices for indoor-outdoor temperature & humidity (see my other reviews) and this one stands out among them for its features, especially ease of use, ease of viewing, and having the right info in the right place.

THE PLUSSES

It's easy to read from a distance; it properly puts temperature first, then humidity; includes a barometer-- and a graph of pressure for the past 24 hours, so you can see if weather is getting fairer or not; and has a Moon phase display which is great for those who enjoy stargazing.

You can also cycle the 24-hour graph through for indoor-outdoor temperature and humidity, too,

We got this one because it has humidity "calibration"-- you can alter the display +- a certain amount. However, we've found both temp and humidity quite accurate. That was gauged by comparing it to a set of regular thermometers and other gauges-- and to itself! You put the sensor next to the device indoors and see if the indoor-outdoor readings match.

The backlit colors are great, too; giving one a feel for the outside temperature by color code.

One big plus-- this operates off both electricity and battery. Best to leave it plugged in. The cord is long enough to put it on a table.

I have been trying to find the perfect weather station, and I think I have!  I have 4 stations now and some are better than others, but finally one with all the features I have been wanting!  The display is easy to read, the set up very easy and the screen color changes by temp  is just great--you will love this feature I promise!  The moon phase is handy, the hi-lows are also perfectly placed, and the charting is spot on--hands down the best part of the unit is the charts/historical graph -- and its very easy to cycle through the different read outs for the graphs and the increments change as the range increases which is just what you want it to do.  This allows you to chart smaller variations or changes.  I only have one teensy "negative", the time and date on the bottom do not show up together--you get on or the other and its difficult to toggle (its actually a setting so you have to go through the entire set up to change it--not feasible really).  I would have settled for no seconds and the date, but its really not too bad--its a weather station after all, not a clock/calendar!

This is NOT an "NSF 53" filter! It is an "NSF 42" filter.

You should note that there are two main levels of filtration, one for taste & odor ("NSF 42") and the other for health and contaminants ("NSF 53"). This filter is the LOWER level filter which may be fine for you but just be aware that this is why it is cheaper than some other OEM filters. If you want to eliminate toxins then get the higher filtration level NSF 53.

NSF 42 filters out: Chlorine
NSF 53 filters out: Chlorine, asbestos, Cyst., Atrazine, Benzine, Lindane, Carbofuran, D-Dichlorbenzene, Lead, Mercury, and other "Particulate class 1" elements.

Also note that this filter is “Tested to NSF Standards” vs NSF Certified, Know the difference. Some products are NSF certified. Some only claim to be “tested to NSF Standards.” What’s the difference? One is actually tested and the other is a marketing claim that is not certified.

The product is a direct replacement for my Kenmore (Lg) refrigerator.  I broke the kenmore filter in half to determine its construction.  It is a compressed tube of powdered activated carbon.  The activated carbon filter does not appear sufficient to remove chlorinated organics ( suspect carcinogen occasionally found in water where organics combine with chlorine disinfectant at the water plant).  It would act to filter particles and would act to remove chlorine ( normal disinfectant found in drinking water)  It might also help with some taste or odor (adsorption by the activated carbon)  I assume this filter has the same internals.  Flow rate is a bit higher which could be from a less compact carbon tube or because the old filter was blocked by turbidity or particles in the water.  I will follow up when this filter is used.
